key_insight: Decision-focused learning enables fast multistage repair decisions, achieving 14%–23% lower costs than the next-best evaluated policy when repair budgets bind.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports rapid power-network repair scheduling under uncertain, time-varying failures and may extend to other structurally similar multistage optimization problems.
method: Predict scores for the sub-decision that drives state transitions using a neural network.
Train on offline single-scenario solutions with a Fenchel–Young loss and perturbed optimization oracles.
Exploit structural conditions under which the scored sub-decision enters the stage objective linearly.
evidence_signal: On common evaluation paths for synthetic 5-bus and IEEE 14-bus networks, DFL led all evaluated policies under binding budgets; its 5-bus mean costs were 1.7%–1.8% above the exact optimum.
watch_item: Benefits depend on problem structure and operating constraints: without a repair budget, DFL did not outperform the near-sighted MPC baseline on the 14-bus network.
paper_title: Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling
